claims.assertion: The only off-route segment is 18:32–18:39, adding 2.21 km; the driver's request to take Outram Road was sent at 18:28 (F7), before that segment started (F3), so the reroute is a single segment under RD-1 and was raised with the rider in advance under RD-5.

The rider never replied to the 18:28 route request (F7, F8); the chat shows no objection message at any time, so there was no consent before the deviation and the segment's extra_km is not exempted by RD-5.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window (F11), and the only congestion evidence is two band-3 (20–29 km/h) records for New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, which are band 3, not band 1 or 2, and are not tied to the substituted stretch of the optimal route; RD-4 therefore gives no exemption for the segment.

Because the segment is unexempted, the rider is entitled to a partial refund on the metered RydeTAXI fare equal to the unexempted segment's extra_km at the trip's per-km rate: 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 (RD-2, using fare fact F4's $1.41/km and the 2.21 extra km in F3).

The refund should be capped at the segment figure and not the whole 3.0 km / $4.21 billed: $4.21 covers the full trip's +3.0 km (F1, F4), whereas the off-route deviation is only 2.21 km (F3), the remainder being route-fitting difference outside any segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded.

The mileage refund operates only on the metered distance units: the waiting line is $0.00 (F6), so no separate time or waiting refund arises under RD-2, and the non-metered allowance rules (FARE-1) do not apply to a RydeTAXI metered trip.

The driver has 752 trips and 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days and no upheld disputes of any kind (F14), so RD-6's 'repeated' condition is not met and no flag_account should attach; the rider's own record shows 2 disputes, 0 upheld (F13).

Fair weather (F12) removed no hazard and created no congestion; the driver's stated reason was building traffic on Kampong Bahru Road, which is supported by no traffic fact at all, so the reroute is unexplained by weather or by any recorded incident.

weaknesses: The rider's account that they did not reply is correct and it is decisive: F7 shows the 18:28 request got no response and F8 is only the driver's self-serving statement, so RD-5 consent fails on the face of the records.

The whole basis for the reroute is the driver's own message about 'traffic building up' on Kampong Bahru Road (F7); F11 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window, and the only speed records (F9, F10) are band 3 on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, i.e. neither band 1 nor 2 and not on the substituted stretch, so RD-4 gives the driver nothing.

The deviation is large and objectively unjustified: F3 shows 3.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km and up to 1262 m away from it, and F1/F2 show the trip 38% / 5.7 minutes longer than estimated, which will read as a clear RD-1 breach on the facts.

The driver's narrative in F8 ('no objection, so I took it') invites the inference of treating silence as consent, which RD-5 and the 'before you go' standard expressly reject, and it is contradicted by the absence of any reply in F7.

Our only real leverage is quantum, not liability: RD-2 allocates only the unexempted segment's extra_km, so we cannot argue the $4.21 billed excess (F4) down to zero, and the rider will press for the full amount charged.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.12 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, Clarke Quay → Sentosa Beach Station, charged $26.46 with a distance line of $15.33 for 10.9 km, so the per-km rate is $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.41/km [F6]. The GPS track shows exactly one off-route segment, 18:32–18:39, where 3.32 km was driven in place of the optimal route's 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km extra_km and straying up to 1262 m from the optimal route [F3]; this is a route deviation that engages the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route duty under RD-1 [F1][F3][RD-1].

The only ground the driver raised for the deviation is his own 18:28 message asking whether he could "go round via Outram Road" [F7]. RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be timestamped before the off-route segment starts, i.e. before 18:32 [F3][F7]. The chat contains only the driver's question; the rider did not reply, and the driver's statement that there was "no objection" is a self-serving characterisation of silence, not a positive agreement [F7][F8]. Silence is not consent, so RD-5 does not exempt the segment [F7][F8][RD-5].

The reasonable-cause defence also fails. No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F11], so RD-4(a) gives nothing. The only congestion evidence, band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway during 18:14–18:54, is neither band 1 nor band 2 nor tied to the substituted stretch of the optimal route, and under RD-4(b) a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. Fair weather adds no hazard [F12][RD-4]. The segment is therefore unexempted.

Because the segment is unexempted, RD-2's metered branch refunds only the extra kilometres of that segment at the trip's per-km rate: 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. I decline to refund the full billed excess of $4.21, which prices the whole trip's +3.0 km [F1][F4]: the segment extra (2.21 km) is smaller than the billed excess (3.0 km), and RD-2 leaves the residual route-fitting difference outside any off-route segment unrefunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. The waiting line is $0.00 and no time or waiting component is claimed, so nothing further arises [F6][RD-2]. No flag_account attaches: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F14], so RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met [F13][F14][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $3.12 SGD to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment, record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file, and remind the driver that route changes require the rider's positive agreement before deviating.

events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your Clarke Quay to Sentosa Beach Station trip and found one part of the route was not the shortest, most direct way. The driver asked you about going via Outram Road, but since you never agreed before the detour began, it doesn't count as exempt. This added about 2.2 km to your fare. We're refunding $3.12 as a Ryde voucher, which will be applied to your account. The rest of your fare stands. Thanks for flagging it.

DRIVER: We reviewed the Clarke Quay to Sentosa Beach Station trip. During part of the journey you took a longer route than the most direct one, and we found no exemption applied: the rider never agreed to the change before the detour, and no traffic incident or qualifying congestion justified it. A route-change breach has been recorded on your file. Remember, route changes need the rider's agreement before you deviate. This is a note on file only — it doesn't affect your account status.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows a single off-route segment from 18:32–18:39 where the driver covered 3.32 km in place of the optimal route's 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km and straying up to 1262 m from the optimal route; the whole trip ran 10.9 km / 22.2 min against an optimal 7.9 km / 16 min (+3.0 km, +38%).
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip charged $26.46, so the 3.0 km of extra driving is billed at $1.41/km, i.e. $4.21 of excess distance fare that must be refunded under RD-2.

The driver never obtained the rider's agreement: the only chat message is the driver's 18:28 question 'ok if I go round via Outram Road?' and the rider's complaint states there was no reply, so the consent requirement of RD-5 (agreement with a timestamp earlier than the segment start) is not met.

The driver's 'reasonable cause' defence fails because there is no traffic incident record near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band evidence (band 3, 20–29 km/h on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway) is neither on the substituted segment of the optimal route nor within the band 1–2 congestion threshold that RD-4 requires.

There is no surge (1.0×) and the fare's only components are base, distance, time, platform fee and zero waiting, so no component of the $26.46 beyond the excess distance is a published charge the rider should bear for this detour; the refund should be limited to the metered excess distance of $4.21.

weaknesses: The driver will argue the rider consented by silence to the Outram Road proposal in chat #1 (F7) and his statement claims 'no objection' (F8); RD-5 requires a positive, timestamped agreement before the segment start, which the chat does not show, but F8 is the evidence the other side will lead.

The driver will point to F9/F10 (band 3, 20–29 km/h on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway during 18:14–18:54) as corroboration of 'building up' traffic, even though RD-4(a) needs an incident record and F11 shows none.
The requested amount is bounded by the fare facts: F4 attributes only $4.21 to the excess distance, so a claim for more than $4.21 of the $26.46 would exceed what the data supports.
The rider's own profile (F13) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld and there is no prior upheld route dispute against this driver (F14), so no account flag is supportable under RD-6.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment is 18:32–18:39, adding 2.21 km; the driver's request to take Outram Road was sent at 18:28 (F7), before that segment started (F3), so the reroute is a single segment under RD-1 and was raised with the rider in advance under RD-5.

The rider never replied to the 18:28 route request (F7, F8); the chat shows no objection message at any time, so there was no consent before the deviation and the segment's extra_km is not exempted by RD-5.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window (F11), and the only congestion evidence is two band-3 (20–29 km/h) records for New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, which are band 3, not band 1 or 2, and are not tied to the substituted stretch of the optimal route; RD-4 therefore gives no exemption for the segment.

Because the segment is unexempted, the rider is entitled to a partial refund on the metered RydeTAXI fare equal to the unexempted segment's extra_km at the trip's per-km rate: 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 (RD-2, using fare fact F4's $1.41/km and the 2.21 extra km in F3).

The refund should be capped at the segment figure and not the whole 3.0 km / $4.21 billed: $4.21 covers the full trip's +3.0 km (F1, F4), whereas the off-route deviation is only 2.21 km (F3), the remainder being route-fitting difference outside any segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded.

The mileage refund operates only on the metered distance units: the waiting line is $0.00 (F6), so no separate time or waiting refund arises under RD-2, and the non-metered allowance rules (FARE-1) do not apply to a RydeTAXI metered trip.

The driver has 752 trips and 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days and no upheld disputes of any kind (F14), so RD-6's 'repeated' condition is not met and no flag_account should attach; the rider's own record shows 2 disputes, 0 upheld (F13).

Fair weather (F12) removed no hazard and created no congestion; the driver's stated reason was building traffic on Kampong Bahru Road, which is supported by no traffic fact at all, so the reroute is unexplained by weather or by any recorded incident.

weaknesses: The rider's account that they did not reply is correct and it is decisive: F7 shows the 18:28 request got no response and F8 is only the driver's self-serving statement, so RD-5 consent fails on the face of the records.

The whole basis for the reroute is the driver's own message about 'traffic building up' on Kampong Bahru Road (F7); F11 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window, and the only speed records (F9, F10) are band 3 on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, i.e. neither band 1 nor 2 and not on the substituted stretch, so RD-4 gives the driver nothing.

The deviation is large and objectively unjustified: F3 shows 3.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km and up to 1262 m away from it, and F1/F2 show the trip 38% / 5.7 minutes longer than estimated, which will read as a clear RD-1 breach on the facts.

The driver's narrative in F8 ('no objection, so I took it') invites the inference of treating silence as consent, which RD-5 and the 'before you go' standard expressly reject, and it is contradicted by the absence of any reply in F7.

Our only real leverage is quantum, not liability: RD-2 allocates only the unexempted segment's extra_km, so we cannot argue the $4.21 billed excess (F4) down to zero, and the rider will press for the full amount charged.

points.response: The 18:28 message (F7) is only a question; RD-5 does not treat a proposal as agreement, it requires the rider's consent message to be timestamped before the segment start, and the driver produced no such consent — F3 fixes the segment start at 18:32.

Conceded as far as it goes: F7/F8 show no rider reply, so the driver's own theory of advance consent collapses under RD-5 — but silence does not excuse the deviation, it makes the segment unexempted and refundable under RD-2.

We agree the segment is unexempted: with no incident record (F11) and only band-3 speeds on other roads (F9, F10), RD-4 gives the driver nothing, and the driver's own 'traffic building up' claim in F7 has no supporting fact.

Partly conceded on arithmetic but not on scope: the per-km rate in F4 is $1.41/km and the segment extra is 2.21 km in F3, yet the refund is the metered excess actually charged for that extra driving — the $4.21 recorded in F4 — since the $3.12 figure leaves part of the billed excess distance unrecovered.

F1 and F4 record a single 3.0 km / $4.21 billed excess for the whole trip, which is less than the 3.32 km actually driven on the unexempted segment in F3, so the billed excess is entirely attributable to the deviation and nothing is left over as map-fitting residue.
Not contested: waiting is $0.00 (F6) and we claim no time or waiting component, only the metered distance excess under RD-2.

Accepted: the driver has 752 trips with 0 upheld disputes (F14) and the rider has 0 upheld disputes (F13), so RD-6's 'repeated' condition is not met and we do not seek flag_account — the finding stands as an RD-1 breach only.

We rely on our own inconsistency, not theirs: F12 fair weather and F11's absence of incidents leave the reroute unexplained under RD-4, which is why the segment is unexempted and its billed excess is refundable.

Concede the fact of the deviation: F1/F2/F3 show one off-route segment 18:32–18:39 adding 2.21 km within a trip +3.0 km / +38%. RD-2 measures the refund per unexempted segment, so liability is limited to 2.21 km, not the 3.0 km the rider's framing implies.

Contested on quantum: RD-2 computes the refund only from the unexempted segment's extra_km (2.21 km in F3), giving 2.21 × $1.41 = $3.12 — not the $4.21 in F4, which prices the whole trip's +3.0 km (F1) and includes mapping-residual distance outside any off-route segment that RD-2 does not refund.

Conceded as to liability on the segment: F7 shows only the 18:28 question with no rider reply and F8 is the driver's own statement, so there is no positive agreement timestamped before the 18:32 segment start as RD-5 requires; the segment is therefore unexempted and draws the RD-2 refund in D4.

Conceded: F11 records no traffic incident near the route in the trip window and F9/F10 are merely band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, neither band 1–2 nor tied to the substituted stretch, so RD-4(a) and (b) give no exemption.

The no-surge finding in F5 and the fare breakdown in F6 do not enlarge the refund: RD-2's metered branch refunds distance units only, and the distance line is 10.9 km in F6, of which only 2.21 km is attributed to the off-route segment by F3; the $4.21 in F4 is the billed excess for the full +3.0 km, and the ≤0.25 km residual under RD-2 stays with the driver.

Withdrawn as far as it seeks an exemption: the pre-segment timing shown by F7 versus F3 satisfies RD-5's 'before you go' chronology but not its agreement element, so the segment stands as unexempted and the per-km refund applies.
My own cap claim stands and is the point of difference with the rider: F1 and F4 price 3.0 km while F3 isolates 2.21 km, so RD-2 supports $3.12 and not $4.21.
